decisions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
decisions.passage: Food, as we all know, is ①essential for human life. It also is the basis for several major industries ②found in many countries around the world such as in agriculture, food processing, food retailing and food service. For millennia, the focus of those involved with food as a human and economic phenomenon was on its production, preservation, distribution, pricing and other practical concerns. But in the late 18th century this began to change. Food became more than just a life necessity. Restaurants began to be developed, ③initial in France but eventually in other nations, as a distinct institution ④offering people dining choices and table service, the opportunity for socialization and, over time, a finer and finer atmosphere. The rise of restaurants eventually led to a class of diners who prided themselves on being critics of taste, food and cooking. Brillat-Savarin is probably the best known of the 'culinary philosophers' or, in today's parlance, a 'foodie'. One of Brillat-Savarin's better known sayings was, '[t]ell me what you eat, and I'll tell you who you are.'
decisions.korean: ③ initial → initially. 부사 위치에 형용사 불가.
decisions.analysis:
✅ ① essential: 형용사, 적절
✅ ② found: 과거분사, 적절
❌ ③ initial → initially: 부사 필요 ←정답
✅ ④ offering: 현재분사, 적절

decisions.stem: 위 글에서 Brillat-Savarin의 유명한 말에 따르면, 무엇을 알려주면 그 사람이 누구인지 알 수 있다고 했는지, 해당 영어 표현을 본문에서 찾아 (영어로) 쓰시오. (3단어)
decisions.korean: 원문: tell me what you eat.
decisions.analysis: 당신이 먹는 것 = what you eat
decisions.tip: tell me what you eat = 무엇을 먹는지 말해줘

decisions.stem: 위 글에서 음식에 대한 관심이 변하기 전, 수천 년 동안의 초점이 무엇이었는지 해당 영어 단어를 본문에서 찾아 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)
